correctness.rationale: For finite \(r\ge p^*\), a weakly null normalized sequence in \(\ell_p\) has a subsequence equivalent to a block basic sequence, hence to the canonical basis. Because \((\ell_p)^*=\ell_{p^*}\subseteq\ell_r\), that subsequence is weakly \(r\)-summable, contradicting weak \(r\)-singularity. Thus any weakly \(r\)-singular maximizing sequence is non-weakly-null, so WMP yields norm attainment. The reverse implication is Proposition 2.1(4) of arXiv:2609.03988v1. Proposition 4.1 gives the perturbation implication and inheritance, while Theorem 2.2 and Examples 4.2 give the sharp \((\ell_p,\ell_p)\) obstruction below \(p^*\). Equality \(r=p^*\) is included because \(\ell_{p^*}\subseteq\ell_r\) remains true at equality.

value.rationale: The result collapses an entire newly introduced hierarchy on the important domain \(\ell_p\): once WMP is known, no additional codomain geometry is needed above the sharp exponent \(p^*\). For WMP codomains containing an isometric \(\ell_p\), the same exponent simultaneously classifies both SMP and convergent perturbations. This turns several isolated target computations into a reusable transfer theorem and identifies which part of the threshold is forced solely by the domain.
